content_voiceover: This page pairs a repeat question on therapy related AML with an ELN 2022 risk stratification question. Question eight's wrong statement claims that ICC 2022 sets therapy related AML apart as its own unique diagnostic entity called myeloid neoplasms post cytotoxic therapy. Actually, the ICC approach attaches post cytotoxic therapy as a qualifier onto the underlying AML diagnosis rather than creating a separate category, that distinction is what the WHO fifth edition does instead. Question sixteen asks which ELN 2022 risk statement is wrong, and it's the one classifying AML with mutated NPM1 plus translocation six nine and DEK NUP214 fusion as intermediate risk. Translocation six nine is an adverse cytogenetic marker under ELN 2022, and it overrides a favorable NPM1 mutation, so this combination should be classified as adverse risk, not intermediate. The other listed scenarios are correctly assigned, bZIP in-frame CEBPA is favorable, wild type NPM1 with high FLT3 ITD allelic ratio is intermediate, mono-allelic TP53 with a measurable variant allele fraction is adverse, and core binding factor AML with t(8;21) and a KIT mutation stays favorable despite the KIT mutation.
keypoints: ICC 2022 treats therapy-related AML as a qualifier, not a separate entity, unlike WHO fifth edition
Translocation six nine with DEK NUP214 is adverse risk under ELN2022, even with NPM1 mutation
bZIP in-frame CEBPA mutation remains favorable risk
KIT mutation does not downgrade core binding factor AML with t(8;21) from favorable
keypoint_voiceover: Don't mix up ICC and WHO on therapy related AML, ICC uses post cytotoxic therapy as a qualifier, WHO fifth edition makes it a separate entity. And for ELN2022 risk, translocation six nine with DEK NUP214 is adverse regardless of NPM1 status, it overrides the otherwise favorable NPM1 mutation. Remember too that a KIT mutation doesn't knock t(8;21) core binding factor AML out of the favorable group.
